minutes.headline: Capital Planning Committee began setting standard presentation rules and scheduled its next meeting for August 21 at 6:30.
minutes.summary: The committee welcomed a new member and discussed what department heads should include in capital request presentations (PowerPoint, per-request slides, cost-benefit analysis for new inventory, age and mileage for replacements). It reviewed ClearGov scoring criteria, considered adding Green Communities and board-endorsement items, and made an introductory review of the draft Financial Policy Manual's capital planning section. The next meeting was set and the meeting adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee reached consensus to ask department heads for a cost-benefit analysis on new inventory requests, and to encourage one for replacements.
For replacements, the committee wants the age and mileage of the item being replaced included in the request presentation.
Green Communities status and endorsement by an overseeing board will be presentation requirements, not part of the ClearGov scoring.
Members were asked to read and mark up the capital planning section of the draft Financial Policy Manual for a future meeting.
The next meeting was set for Wednesday, August 21, at 6:30; no votes were taken at this meeting.

why_it_matters: These rules set what a department must show to have a capital request (a vehicle, equipment, a building project) ranked, and how the committee's ranking is built.
The committee only ranks requests; the town manager sets the capital figure from free cash and other sources, so the ranking sets the order of the list but not how much is spent.
